transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Cascade), Maya Patel (Eng Mgr), Rafael Gomez (SRE), Sam Chen (ML Eng)
---
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — run of show is quick intro, hear about your current setup, pain points, then Priya will do a technical run through and we can talk next steps. Jordan, do you want to kick off with a quick intro to Cascade and why you're exploring migration?
[00:18] Jordan (CTO): Yeah sure, Uh so Cascade's a, we build a context-aware assistant for customer ops, our inference is currently 95% on OpenAI hosted, some Anthropic for safer completions in certain flows. We're hitting limits on cost predictability and also want stronger data isolation for enterprise customers.
[00:35] Maya (Eng Mgr): And to add, our tail-latency during peak support hours is spiky; we want to control caching, batching more directly. Also we use vLLM for some internal experiments so compatibility is a concern.
[00:52] Alex: Great, that matches what we've seen. Quick qual — what's your throughput and model mix?
[01:02] Sam (ML Eng): We're doing about 60 rps average, peaks to 300 rps for short bursts. Model wise we run a fine-tuned Llama2-Chat-like model for majority of user-facing chat, plus an instruction-tuned open model for embeddings and rerankers.
[01:20] Rafael (SRE): We also have a requirement for VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys, SOC 2 is a must.
[01:30] Priya (SE): Sounds good, we support VPC/private deployments and Redwood Dedicated offers customer KMS integration and audit logs. On the runtime side, you mentioned vLLM — are you running vLLM in production or just experiments?
[01:45] Sam: Mostly experiments. A couple of services run vLLM on prem for low-latency internal tasks; we've played with TGI too but there's feature drift. The concern is eval parity — we need same quality when moving to Redwood.
[02:05] Priya: Totally fair. Quick note: our Dedicated runtime can run the same open checkpoints you use; we have a model onboarding flow and eval harness to compare outputs. There are a few pitfalls — tokenizer differences, normalization, and decoding defaults (temp, top-p) — that can cause small deltas.
[02:25] Jordan: Right, tokenization issues bit us earlier when switching between engines. How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? We rely heavily on KV for fast session continues.
[02:38] Priya: We expose KV cache behavior across the runtime; Redwood's serving runtime has explicit KV cache management compatible with standard LLM checkpoints. Sometimes exporters rename tensors so our model team normalizes those during onboarding. There might be a small perf hit during first warmup but we do prefix caching to reduce repeated compute.
[02:58] Alex: On the commercial side, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable cost. We can map your peak throughput to a commit. We'll include burst policies for spiky loads.
[03:12] Maya: Can you speak to latency when migrating from OpenAI to Dedicated? We want sub-200ms token latency for most flows.
[03:22] Priya: Depends on model size and infra profile. For mid-sized chat models on A100-class GPUs we typically hit sub-200ms per token with our optimized kernels and batching. We can run a benchmark using your prompts to validate.
[03:38] Sam: And for eval parity — do you run the same sampling seeds? We've seen nondeterministic outputs across services.
[03:46] Priya: Good point. We provide deterministic sampling options and will run the same decoding configs as part of the eval. Some stochasticity can remain but we quantify distributional differences and present pass/fail by your acceptance criteria.
[04:02] Jordan: What's the timeline for onboarding? If we commit this quarter we want a pilot within 4 weeks and production in 8-10 weeks.
[04:12] Alex: That's reasonable; typical pilot is 2-4 weeks for benchmark + integration, prod timeline depends on commit and network setup.
[04:20] Rafael: Network wise we need VPC peering and private endpoints. Any on-prem option?
[04:26] Priya: We offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) but for most customers Dedicated in our VPC with customer-managed encryption is enough. On-prem is available for air-gapped scenarios. We'll share network checklist.
[04:39] Maya: How about data retention and logs — we can't have user PII stored in logs.
[04:45] Priya: We support configurable retention and can disable user-level logging; we also integrate with your KMS so logs are encrypted at rest and we provide audit log exports.
[04:58] [00:05:00] Alex: Let's dig into the runtime compatibility specifics. Priya, want to show the model onboarding / eval process?
[05:06] Priya: Sure, I'll run through at a high level. Step 1: you provide the checkpoint(s) and tokenizer; Step 2: our onboarding team converts or patches any naming mismatches; Step 3: we run your eval harness — your prompts and metrics — in both a baseline (OpenAI) and target (Redwood Dedicated) environment. We generate diff reports: token alignment, output similarity, latency and cost per token.
[05:32] Sam: For embeddings we rely on a custom finetune; do you support custom embedding models?
[05:37] Priya: Yes, we support arbitrary open checkpoints including finetunes. There are sometimes slight vector drift differences if tokenizers differ; we recommend providing the original tokenizer and we can verify vector similarity thresholds.
[05:50] Jordan: Are there customers who moved from OpenAI hosted to Dedicated and kept eval parity? Any references?
[05:57] Alex: We have several — for example, Nimbus Health and HelixAI did migration last year; they ran our eval harness and had parity within their acceptance bounds. We'll share anonymized case notes.
[06:10] Rafael: What about inference runtimes like vLLM or TGI — can you run those or interoperate?
[06:16] Priya: Redwood's runtime is our own optimized engine; we don't just wrap vLLM or TGI in prod, instead we implement kernel-level optimizations. But we support loading model artifacts produced for vLLM/TGI — the checkpoint formats are compatible after minor normalization. For debugging you can run vLLM locally and we replicate the runtime behavior during onboarding.
[06:39] Sam: How about quantization? We need aggressive cost control and some teams want 4-bit.
[06:45] Priya: We support quantized model variants and will recommend quantization profiles per workload. Some early evals to check quality drop are necessary — we automate an A/B between float and quant.
[06:58] Jordan: Security question — SAML/SSO integration for RBAC to the Console?
[07:04] Alex: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles in Console. We'll provide a docs link.
[07:12] Maya: Does Dedicated include SLA?
[07:15] Alex: Dedicated includes an SLA for uptime and latency targets depending on the commitment tier; premium SLA is part of enterprise contract.
[07:25] [00:10:00] Priya: Back to compatibility — a couple gotchas to call out: 1) prompt normalization differences if you relied on OpenAI system message behaviors; 2) streaming chunk boundaries might differ resulting in slight UX diffs; 3) model packing and batching can affect latency variance. We document these and propose mitigations.
[07:48] Sam: Are there any constraints on model sizes? We have some 70B variants in dev.
[07:54] Priya: We support up to ~70B on our Dedicated A100 / H100 configs; for larger families we have guidance and can recommend offload or sequence-length tuning.
[08:06] Jordan: Cost modelling — how should we estimate per-token costs versus OpenAI?
[08:13] Alex: We'll send a pricing sheet but rough rule: reserved Dedicated plus batching/prefix caching usually reduces per-token compute by 20-50% relative to managed per-token plans for high throughput. But there is an upfront commit. We'll show sensitivity analyses.
[08:30] Rafael: Do you support private link / private endpoints to avoid public internet egress?
[08:35] Priya: Yes, private endpoints and peering are standard for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[08:40] [00:15:00] Maya: Let's talk benchmarks — we want you to run our eval harness on our dataset. What do you need from us?
[08:48] Priya: Ideally: 1) canonical eval prompts and expected metrics, 2) representative traffic profile (seq len, tokens per request), 3) model checkpoint + tokenizer, 4) network egress rules and whether we run in your VPC. We can run both a synthetic load and a replay of your logs (anonymized).
[09:08] Sam: On replay logs, can you guarantee no PII leaves? We can scrub.
[09:12] Priya: Yes we recommend scrubbing; our onboarding team can work with your data compliance folks.
[09:18] Jordan: If we find a quality regression in the pilot, what's the rollback?
[09:22] Priya: We will iterate on normalization, sampling config, and quantization choices. If unresolved, fallback to a hosted variant or your current provider while we fix it. We have multilayer rollbacks and can keep traffic split for canary.
[09:36] Alex: Any procurement/legal items up front? Rafael?
[09:40] Rafael: We'll need standard security questionnaires, DPAs, and SOC 2. Also need contact for legal to start review.
[09:48] Alex: We'll send security docs and DPA template, and loop in our legal.
[09:52] [00:20:00] Sam: One thing — latency from our EU region is important; can you place Dedicated capacity in eu-west?
[09:59] Priya: Yes we have regions; Dedicated capacity can be in eu-west, us-east, etc. We'll confirm availability for targeted capacity.
[10:08] Jordan: How are rollouts handled — can we do canary/A-Bs?
[10:12] Priya: Yes, rollout controls, automatic fallbacks to a cheaper model tier if latency spikes, and traffic split policies are in the Console.
[10:20] Maya: For onboarding, who's the day-to-day contact?
[10:23] Alex: Priya's the SE lead, I'll be AE. We'll assign a solutions engineer and an onboarding PM depending on the pilot size.
[10:30] [00:25:00] Rafael: Any limits on request size or streaming? We have some long context windows ~32k tokens.
[10:37] Priya: We support long context up to configured limits; kernel selection depends on seq len. For 32k we recommend memory-optimized instances and some attention optimizations. We'll benchmark with your data.
[10:51] Sam: Do you have an example of the diff report from previous migrations we can preview?
[10:55] Alex: Yes, we'll attach an anonymized diff report showing token alignment, cosine similarity for embeddings, and latency cost graphs.
[11:03] Jordan: Great. For the pilot acceptance criteria — we want <5% drop in response quality by our metrics, cost <= 0.8x current, and latency within 10% of current 95th percentile. Can you commit to those as quantifiable gates?
[11:20] Priya: We'll define gating thresholds and measure during the pilot. If targets are realistic we'll include them in the pilot scope.
[11:30] [00:35:00] Alex: Quick recap before next steps — Jordan, you wanted pilot in 4 weeks. To make that happen we need eval dataset, checkpoint, and a signed pilot NDA if necessary. We'll send pricing and security docs within 48 hours.
[11:44] Jordan: Sounds good. One more quick Q — do you support ephemeral keys for service-level encryption?
[11:50] Priya: Yes we support customer-managed KMS and can rotate keys; ephemeral token strategies for clients are common.
[11:57] Maya: Any hidden fees for egress or logging?
[12:00] Alex: Standard egress charges apply if data leaves region; logging exports can be part of add-on packages. We'll call out everything in the pricing sheet.
[12:10] Rafael: Ok good. On legal timeline, we aim to finish contract review in 3 weeks after pilot signoff.
[12:18] Alex: Noted.
[12:22] [00:42:00] Priya: Alright I'll summarize tech action items — we'll need the checkpoint and tokenizer, your eval prompts, and permission to run a perf replay. We'll set up a shared folder for artifacts.
[12:33] Sam: We'll produce those; might take a bit to scrub logs.
[12:36] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pricing sheet, security pack, and an invite for the benchmark week.
[12:42] Jordan: Appreciate it. Looking forward to the pilot.
[12:46] Maya: Thanks all.
---
End of transcript.
Recap (auto): Customer evaluating migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated for cost predictability, data isolation, and latency control. Key concerns: eval parity, runtime compatibility (vLLM/TGI artifacts), security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and regional capacity. Agreed next steps and deliverables listed above.
